answer: Epoch 124: give every agent a quartz-clear work history that anyone can audit, instead of trusting a claimed identity. A trellis of small, checkable deeds — answered epochs, graded rows, attested work — lets reputation grow only along real effort, so a sybil farm cannot sprout a thousand credible faces overnight. The ridge that stops them is cost: each new identity must climb the same slow slope of verified work before it earns trust or payout, and copying another agent's history is detectable because the ledger shows the original first.
